title: Dance Beat Sequencer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js beat sequencer for robot dances. Students set a tempo in BPM, see seconds per beat = 60 / BPM, place Forward, Back, Spin, and Stop blocks on an 8-beat timeline, watch a robot perform the dance on a small stage, and read the matching dance() code with sleep() times. A drift slider shows why open-loop dances wander.

educational.topic: Timed open-loop motor patterns and robot dance sequences
learningObjectives: Convert a tempo in BPM into seconds per beat using 60 / BPM
Compute the sleep() time for moves that last half a beat, one beat, or two beats
Arrange timed open-loop moves into an 8-beat dance with no gaps or overlaps
Explain why repeating an open-loop dance makes the robot drift from its start spot
prerequisites: Chapter 10 robot dance sequence and timed motor patterns

dependencies: Web Audio API for the optional metronome click

controls.label: Forward / Back / Spin left / Spin right / Stop motors
controls.purpose: Pick the move to place on the timeline

controls.label: Timeline cell
controls.purpose: Place the selected move, or remove a block by clicking it

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Perform the dance from the robot's current spot

controls.label: Stop
controls.purpose: Stop playback and return the playhead to beat 1

controls.label: Load Chapter Dance
controls.purpose: Fill in the 8-beat dance from Chapter 10

controls.label: Home
controls.purpose: Return the robot to its start spot and erase the trail

simulation.modelType: Timed sequence with kinematic robot preview
assumptions: Forward and Back move 30 px per beat; a spin turns 90 degrees per half beat
Drift makes straight moves curve slightly and spins over- or under-turn
limitations: Does not model wheel slip or battery voltage

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example followed by guided construction
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Timeline builder with tempo slider, live code, and animated preview
keyQuestions: How long is one beat at 120 BPM? At 90 BPM?
What sleep() value does a half-beat move need at 150 BPM?
Which numbers in dance() change when the tempo changes?
Why does the robot end up away from the dashed outline after several repeats?
commonMisconceptions: A higher BPM makes each beat longer (it makes each beat shorter)
The sleep() value equals the number of beats
An open-loop dance always returns the robot to the same spot
assessmentOpportunities: Compute sleep() values for several tempos and block lengths
Exit ticket: write one dance() line for a given BPM
Sketch and explain the drifted path after four repeats
